Shattered Legacy's own art for TazUO, shipped in the player package (cc-P26, F-8)
================================================================================

What is here
------------
  art\<id>.png    art overrides, by static item ID in decimal. The build copies them to
                  app\tazuo\ExternalImages\art\, where TazUO draws them instead of the art in the
                  player's artLegacyMUL.uop (TazUO ExternalImageLoader.Load and Art.LoadSourceArtInfo).
  registry.csv    every ID we use, one row each, with its kind: art (an art/item ID), anim (an Animation
                  number), gump (a gump ID) or body (a creature body, cc-P139). scripts\find-free-art.py reads it so a later pack never
                  takes one of these IDs, and --check-registry re-tests each in its own space.
  records.json    our tiledata and animdata records for the IDs that need them, our worn-item
                  animations (equipAnims) and our creature bodies (bodyAnims, cc-P139). The build copies it to app\art-records.json. Play.ps1 writes
                  it into copies of the player's own tiledata.mul, animdata.mul and Bodyconv.def
                  (app\uo-overrides\), never into the player's EA files.
                  Nothing of EA's is shipped: not a file, not a part of one.
  gumps\<id>.png  gump overrides (cc-P62), into app\tazuo\ExternalImages\gumps\ beside Fiddle-Me-This's.
  anim-src\bodies\<body>.vd
                  a creature body's frames as a UOFiddler .vd (cc-P139), copied block for block into
                  sl-anim7.bin at the anim7 slot records.json's bodyAnims gives it.
  anim-src\<N>\a<action>_d<direction>_f<frame>.png
                  the frames of worn-item animation N, 130 x 128, canvas (x, y) = run coordinates
                  (x - 67, y - 98). scripts\build-equip-anims.py encodes them into sl-anim7.bin and
                  sl-anim7-idx.bin (committed; --check proves they are what the PNGs build), which ship
                  as app\sl-anim7.bin and app\sl-anim7-idx.bin and which TazUO reads as anim7.mul/.idx.

Burrow scamp slinger, creature body 2048 (0x800) (cc-P139, F-46; F-45's archer)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Author:      Vert-I-Go, "Kobold-Bow", https://www.servuo.dev/archive/kobold-bow.2532/ (posted 2025-11-21).
             The author's description: "Kobold with bow attack animation from Baldurs gate." A Baldur's Gate rip.
Downloaded:  2026-10-13 by the daily art task. Original at D:\UO\third-party\kobold-bow\ (Kobold Bow.vd, 159,223 bytes).
License:     NO LICENSE STATED. Cleared by Chase 2026-10-15: rip allowed, renamed in game (every creature on it gets
             our own name; "kobold" is a Wizards of the Coast name and is not used in game). Credit Vert-I-Go; ship
             only inside the player package or the private repo; do not repost.
  anim-src\bodies\2048.vd   the download, byte for byte (SHA-256 be548c1f5527c1d7485410c412a2575d45a171a310dab133c0c8c2e1114ff0fd).
                            A UOFiddler .vd: high (monster) layout, 22 actions x 5 directions, 40 blocks with frames
                            (actions 0 walk, 1 stand, 2 and 3 die, 4 attack (the bow shot), 10 get hit, 17 and 18
                            fidget), 185 frames. scripts\build-equip-anims.py copies each block unchanged into
                            sl-anim7.bin at anim7 slot 1 (records.json bodyAnims); the launcher adds
                            "2048 -1 -1 -1 -1 -1 1" to its copy of the player's Bodyconv.def and "2048 MONSTER 0" to
                            its copy of mobtypes.txt. The server types body 2048 Monster (ShardBodyTypes.cs).

build\sl-anim7.bin at the anim7 slot records.json's bodyAnims gives it (scripts\build-equip-anims.py). Every
pack below is in D:\UO\third-party\<folder>\ with its own SOURCE.txt; the terms there apply. Game rips are
allowed since Chase's 2026-10-15 call, and every creature has an in-game name of ours (no Wizards of the Coast
names in game). Credit the author; ship only inside the player package or the private repo; do not repost.

(the Crop Crow) is EA's stock bird body 6 at 1.5x, both by the Burrows Bestiary renderer's EPX scale2x then a
BOX resize (notes\art\bestiary\up.py), alpha cut at 128, colours median-cut to 256 a block and snapped to 15
bits (cc-P140 notes, Part B). The crow is EA-derived and ships only as encoded blocks, as the EA-derived PNG art does.
Not registered: the three Tree Fellows (Rootling) are 213 to 390 px tall and 6 to 17 MB each (over the 5 MB
rule); the Rootling wears a hued stock body instead (cc-P140 notes).

Shattered runestone (IDs 15376-15419, 0x3C10-0x3C3B)
----------------------------------------------------
Author:      Vrark
Resource:    "Animated Runestone", https://www.servuo.dev/archive/animated-runestone.2564/
             Posted 2025-12-27. Its description in full: "An animated runestone in four directions."
Downloaded:  2026-09-30, by Chase (logged in to servuo.dev). Original download kept at
             D:\UO\third-party\animated-runestone\ ("MMH7 runestone.zip": four GIFs and four zips of PNGs).
License:     NO LICENSE STATED, in the download or on the page. Posted for the ServUO community to use.
             The download's folder and file names ("MMH7 runestone", "MM7H runestone 2") are a
             misnaming, not a sign of where the art came from. Cleared for use, and to ship to
             players, by Chase on 2026-10-02 ("the art is fine just missnamed"; shard-migration
             notes\p26-decisions-2026-10-02.md, item 1).

The four "designs" are Vrark's four directions of the one stone:
  design 1  15376-15386  Test1_0001_top.png .. Test1_0011_top.png  (MMH7 runestone 1.zip)
  design 2  15387-15397  Test2_0001_top.png .. Test2_0011_top.png  (MM7H runestone 2.zip, folder TOP\)
  design 3  15398-15408  Test3_0001_top.png .. Test3_0011_top.png  (MMH7 runestone 3.zip)
  design 4  15409-15419  Test4_0001_top.png .. Test4_0011_top.png  (MMH7 runestone 4.zip)
Each base ID (the first of each run) is the item's ID and the only one with records. The other ten
are frames only.

Changed from the download, and only this: each design's frames were cut to the union of their
non-transparent pixels (the same cut for all 11, so they stay registered), then given 22 transparent
rows below. That puts the floating stone over the centre of its tile; TazUO puts an image's bottom row
on the tile's bottom tip and its middle column on the tile's centre. No pixel was scaled or altered:
scripts\anchor-art-frames.py checks every frame it writes against its source, pixel for pixel. Before
that, the 44 PNGs were checked byte-identical to the ones in Vrark's four zips.

  python scripts\anchor-art-frames.py --src D:\UO\third-party\animated-runestone\frames\stone<N>
      --first-id <base> --out player-package\vendor\shattered-legacy-art\art --bottom-pad 22

Frame timing: the GIFs run 80 to 90 ms a frame. TazUO's static animation step is
FrameInterval x 100 ms (AnimatedStaticsManager.Process, ITEM_EFFECT_ANIMATION_DELAY 50, doubled), so
records.json uses interval 1: about 100 ms a frame, a little slower than the GIFs.

Tiledata record: copied from OSI's own animated runestone, 0xADBA "Runestone01 Glow01", as read from
the client's tiledata.mul on 2026-10-01: flags 0x01040040 (Animation, PartialHue, Impassable),
weight 1, height 3. Only the name ("shattered runestone") is ours. The flag values are facts about how
OSI's item behaves, not EA data shipped: the record is written by hand here.

Fox ears and tail (cc-P62, F-35): item 15420 (0x3C3C), Animation 4783, gumps 64783 and 54783
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Author:      drawn for Shattered Legacy by the art chat for Chase, 2026-10-05 ("Moonrunner": tall pointed
             ears with dark tips, one long low tail with a cream tip). Ours. Source files, never edited
             here: D:\ShatteredLegacy\design\kitsune-ears-tail\.
  art\15420.png               icon_44.png, byte for byte
  gumps\64783.png             stage2-final\paperdoll_260x237.png with its ears and tail components moved
                              (+2, -25) and (0, -14) to sit on the Siege of Sosaria female body 13 (and the
                              elf 15), cc-P138 (notes\cc-P138-scratch\refit_gumps.py in the docs repo).
                              The P62 file was placed for EA's body 13, whose head is 25 rows lower.
                              cc-P166: the ears 3 rows lower again, to rest on a bald scalp
                              (notes\cc-P166-scratch\lower_paperdoll_ears.py).
  gumps\54783.png             the same art moved (+2, -28) and (0, -16) for the male bodies 12 and 14
                              (50000 + 4783), cc-P138; cc-P166 the ears 2 rows lower.
  paperdoll-fit.json          where each gump must sit on each body; scripts\check-paperdoll-fit.py checks
                              it and Build-PlayerPackage.ps1 refuses to build when it fails (cc-P138).
  anim-src\4783\a00_d1_fNN    stage3-final\walk_dir1\walk_dir1_fNN.png, byte for byte: action 0 (walk
                              unarmed), animation direction 1, frames 0 to 9. Drawn over body 401's own
                              walk frames, so frame i lines up with body 401's frame i.
  anim-src\4783\a00_d{0,2,3,4}_fNN   stage4-final\walk_dirD\walk_dirD_fNN.png (2026-10-06), the stage-4
                              generator's walk frames for the other four drawn directions.
  anim-src\4783\a04_dD_f00   stand (action 4) and
  anim-src\4783\a02_dD_fNN   run (action 2): cc-P138, the same ears and tail placed on those poses by the
                              per-frame guides (direction 1 moved from the walk art, the others from the
                              stage-4 generator), notes\cc-P138-scratch\build_stand_run.py in the docs repo.
  cc-P166 (notes\cc-P166-scratch\build_west.py): drawn direction 3 (server West, North mirrored) redrawn
                              in walk, run and stand with a new tail path (out behind her past the hip, not
                              flat down her legs), and every frame's ears 1 row lower (bald heads).
Natural colours (hue 0); the _partialhue and _gray versions beside them are for later. Not drawn yet:
every other action (war-mode walk and run, fidgets, attacks, ...); they draw nothing. The spec for them is
notes\art\kitsune-ears-tail-remaining-actions.md in the docs repo.
Encoding (scripts\build-equip-anims.py) changes only colour depth: the anim format holds 5 bits a
channel, so each colour becomes the nearest one TazUO can draw (largest difference 4 of 255). Pixel
positions are unchanged.
Tiledata record (records.json): flags 0x00400002 (Wearable, and 0x2, which pinned names Weapon and nothing reads),
weight 1, layer 0x12 (Earrings), height 1, as OSI's earrings 0x1087 read from the client's tiledata.mul on 2026-10-05;
animId 4783 and the name ("fox ears and tail") are ours.

Winter decor (cc-P34, F-22): IDs 15424-15470 (0x3C40-0x3C6E)
--------------------------------------------------------------
Two community packs, downloaded 2026-09-30 by Chase and kept at D:\UO\third-party\winter-holiday\
(originals in _zips\, contact sheets sheet-*.png). Neither pack carries a license file, and neither page
states one: LICENSE NONE STATED. Credit both authors wherever the shard credits art.
  MrRiots, "Winter/Christmas Related stuff" (2024), https://www.servuo.dev/archive/mrriots-winter-christmas-related-stuff.2388/
           folder "For ServUO 2": the animated Father Christmas statue, raised firepit and two stoves, the
           candy cane arches, holiday food, snow-covered paintings and shields, and snow patches.
  Vrark,   "Christmas sprites" (2025), https://www.servuo.dev/archive/christmas-sprites.2545/
           folder "Christmas sprites\BMP": the Christmas tree, Santa's bag, three presents, the Christmas
           fireplace, two garlands, four holiday paintings and the sleigh.
           Vrark's two animated Christmas trees are NOT used: his page says they come from other games.
Every ID's file is in registry.csv. The frames of the animated pieces, in order:
  15424-15428  father christmas   MrRiots Statues\Father Christmas\1.bmp .. 5.bmp (one facing of two)
  15429-15433  raised firepit     MrRiots Raised Firepit\1.bmp .. 5.bmp
  15434-15437  iron stove         MrRiots Stoves\1\1.bmp .. 4.bmp (one facing of two)
  15438-15441  stone stove        MrRiots Stoves\2\1.bmp .. 4.bmp (one facing of two)
What was done to the pixels (notes\cc-P34-tools\convert_art.py, scripts\anchor-art-frames.py
--keep-geometry --black-transparent): the 24-bit BMP became a PNG, and pure black (0,0,0) became
transparent, as UO art means it. Nothing else: no recolouring, no scaling, no redrawing, no cut and no
pad (both authors laid their art out on the canvas the way the art file holds it). Near-black pixels stay
opaque. The tool re-reads every PNG and checks it against its source.
Records (records.json), written by hand, the flags from OSI's own art as read from the client's
tiledata.mul on 2026-10-12: father christmas 0x01004040 height 20 (OSI's statue 0x1224 is 0x4000 and
height 0; ours adds Animation and Impassable so the statue blocks); raised firepit 0x01806240 height 0
(OSI's animated fire pit 0x29FD); iron and stone stove 0x0180A050 height 20 (OSI's animated oven 0x462,
height ours); christmas tree 0x00004041 height 20 (OSI's tree 0xCCA); christmas fireplace 0x00006050
height 20 (OSI's fireplace 0x45D); christmas sleigh 0x00004040 height 10 (ours). Animdata: frames
0..n-1, interval 2, as OSI's fire 0x19AB and campfire 0xDE3 (about 200 ms a frame). The packs give no
timing of their own.

Chest mimic (cc-P50, F-32): IDs 15472-15489 (0x3C70-0x3C81)
------------------------------------------------------------
Author:      Archaaz
Resource:    "Animated Mimic", https://www.servuo.dev/threads/animated-mimic.12406/ (posted 2020-04-07)
Downloaded:  2026-10-03, by Chase (logged in to servuo.dev), file Mimic.7z. Kept at
             D:\UO\third-party\animated-mimic\ (original in _zips\, notes in SOURCE.txt there).
License:     NONE STATED, on the page or in the download. Community art: credit Archaaz, ship it only
             inside the player package, never repost the files. The author made it by modifying EA's own
             chest, slith tongue and tooth graphics, so it ships as our PNGs drawn over placeholder IDs,
             never as a part of an EA file (shard-migration notes\client-policy-2026-10-02.md).
Archaaz's frame 1 (closed) is, pixel for pixel, the stock wooden chest: 0xE43 for the NS frames and
0xE42 for the WE ones (compared on 2026-10-12 in 5-bit colour, 0 pixels differ). So the shard draws the
closed mimic with the stock art and ships only frames 2 to 6 and the two dead frames, per facing:
  +0..+4  stills: teeth showing, mouth open, tongue out 1-3  Animations NS|WE\2.bmp .. 6.bmp
  +5, +6  idle loop (base +5, frames 2 and 3 again)           Animations NS|WE\2.bmp, 3.bmp
  +7      dead, lid flung open                               Extra\6.bmp (NS), Extra\5.bmp (WE)
  +8      dead, tongue out                                   Extra\8.bmp (NS), Extra\7.bmp (WE)
  NS at 15472-15480, WE at 15481-15489. The lid alone (Extra 1-2) and the spike-trap chest (Extra 3-4)
  are not used (the spike chest is noted for F-32's trapped chests).
What was done to the pixels (shard-migration notes\cc-P50-tools\convert_art.py, then
scripts\anchor-art-frames.py --keep-geometry --black-transparent): BMP to PNG, pure black (0,0,0) to
transparent. Placement only, no pixel of the art changed: the WE frames get 4 transparent rows underneath
(stock 0xE42 has 16 empty rows under its art, Archaaz's WE frames 12), and the wider dead frames get
transparent columns on one side and lose empty bottom rows so the chest body stands where the stock chest
stands. The tool re-reads every PNG and checks it against its (placed) source.
Records (records.json), written by hand: every still and the loop base 0x00004040 (Impassable | ArticleA)
height 4 weight 255, as OSI's wooden chest 0xE43 (0x00204040) without Container; the loop base adds
Animation (0x01004040); the dead tiles 0x00004000 (ArticleA), height 4. Animdata: the loop base, frames
0 and 1, interval 4 (about 400 ms a frame, twice the winter fire's 2). Server copy: ChestMimicArt.Records.

Achievements paperdoll button, gumps 22456 (normal), 22457 (pressed), 22458 (hover) (cc-P147)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A PLACEHOLDER until Chase's art chat draws the real one (brief: shard-migration notes\art\achievements-button\BRIEF.md).

             label cleared; the label "Achievements" drawn in Arial Narrow Bold in the Help button's own label colours.
Style:       Castiel, "Classic Desktop Missing Paperdoll buttons" (servuo.dev 1519), gumps 22450 to 22455, the Quests and
             Guild buttons; our IDs follow his. Credit Castiel.
Made by:     notes\art\achievements-button\make_button.py in shard-migration (reproducible from the package's own art).

             shard. Other clients never ask for these IDs.

New Haven community art (cc-P237, F-21): IDs 15496-15529 (0x3C88-0x3CA9)
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
Seven community packs Chase approved for New Haven (F-21, 2026-09-30: "decorate New Haven appropriately with these
packs"), each kept in its own folder under D:\UO\third-party\ (originals in _zips\). None carries a license file.
Community work: credit the author wherever the shard credits art, ship it only inside the player package, never
repost the files.
  Moonrose,     "Farm carts", servuo.dev (folder farm-carts; it has no SOURCE.txt, README.md there says
                "Moonrose, none stated"): a fruit cart and a vegetable cart, two facings each. Made for OSI's
                placeholder slots 6784, 6785, 6807 and 6808; shipped here at new IDs (find-free-art.py reports a
                false code hit on 6808, a line number in a comment, and one block keeps the set together).
  Ems,          "Oil lantern", https://www.servuo.dev/archive/oil-lantern.2592/ : three lit frames (lantern 1-3);
                lantern 4 (unlit) is not used.
  OUTLANDSOwyn, "Marble Railings, Bannisters, Ladder", https://www.servuo.dev/archive/marble-railings-bannisters-ladder.2663/ :
                two pieces, his 70321 (straight railing) and 70324 (railing with its end post).
  gollin,       "Bridge support beam 1.0", https://www.servuo.dev/archive/bridge-support-beam.2396/ : the four
                supports (east-west and north-south, left and right); the two bottom beams are not used.
  Vrark,        "Orc encampment 1", https://www.servuo.dev/archive/orc-encampment.2395/ ("you are welcome to do with
                as you wish"; he asks to see it on the shard): his finished BMPs 0xB2B3 (cage), 0xB2B8 (campfire),
                0xB2BB (meat rack), 0xB2BF and 0xB2C0 (palisade), 0xB2C3 (rug), 0xB2C7, 0xB2CB and 0xB2CF (tents).
  Odin,         "Paintings", https://www.servuo.dev/archive/paintings.2351/ and "Nightmare & The Magic Circle",
                https://www.servuo.dev/archive/nightmare-the-magic-circle.2375/ : all twelve, public-domain paintings.
Every ID's file is in registry.csv. The lantern's frames, in order: 15500-15502 lantern 1.bmp, 2.bmp, 3.bmp.
What was done to the pixels (shard-migration notes\cc-P237-tools\convert_art.py, scripts\anchor-art-frames.py
--keep-geometry): the format only. The 24-bit BMPs (beams, the orc camp, the paintings) also had pure black (0,0,0)
made transparent (--black-transparent), as UO art means it; the carts (TIFF), lantern (32-bit BMP) and railings (PNG)
carry their own alpha and keep every pixel. No cut, no pad, no scaling: each author laid the art out on the canvas the
way the art file holds it. The tool re-reads every PNG and checks it against its source.
Records (records.json; the server's copy is ClusterFCommunityArtRecords.Records), the flags from OSI's own art as
read from the client's tiledata.mul on 2026-10-21: carts 0x00004040 height 3 (OSI's ore cart 0x1A82, ArticleA);
oil lantern 0x01808000 light 2 height 2 (OSI's lantern 0x0A15 without Wearable), animdata frames 0,1,2,1,0,0,1,0
interval 6 (0x0A15's own; the pack gives no timing); marble railings 0x00004044 height 5 (OSI's wooden banister
0x08AE); support beams 0x04000050 height 16 (OSI's wood supports 0x019C); orcish palisade 0x0400A050 height 20 (OSI's
palisade 0x0221 without Damaging); orcish tents and hut 0x0000A050 height 20 (OSI's tent wall 0x01F0, ArticleAn);
orcish campfire 0x00808000 light 29 height 1 (OSI's campfire 0x0DE3 without Animation and Damaging); orcish cage
0x00008040 height 20 and meat rack 0x00008040 height 15 (ours). The rug and the paintings are walk-through and need no
record.

Satchel and guild bag icons, art 13184-13189 (0x3380-0x3385) (cc-P236)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
Author:      Chase (Shattered Legacy), from his own source art; Codex drew the 44x40 icons, 2026-10-05. Approved by
             Chase 2026-10-05 (shard-migration docs\feature-queue.md, "Satchel icons").
License:     OURS. No credit owed to anyone else; credit line if one is wanted: "Satchel icons: Chase, Shattered Legacy".
Files:       D:\ShatteredLegacy\design\satchel-icons\<name>.png, copied byte for byte (no pixel changed):
               13184 ore_satchel.png              CompactOreSatchel and tiers T2 to T5
               13185 lumber_satchel.png           ForestersLumberSatchel, SeasonedLumberSatchel, ArboristLumberSatchel
               13186 hunters_satchel.png          HuntersSatchel, SeasonedHuntersSatchel, WardensFieldSatchel
               13187 artificers_satchel.png       ArtificersSatchel (hue 0xDC, Chase 2026-10-05)
               13188 gemologists_satchel.png      GemologistsSatchel
               13189 smith_guild_salvage_bag.png  SmithGuildSalvageBag
             The icons hold exact grays (R = G = B) where the hue goes, so with PartialHue a tier hue tints only those.
Not shipped (approved, no item yet): arcane_society_reagent_pouch (hue 0x12B decided), tailors_cloth_satchel,
             maritime_fishers_creel, healers_covenant_satchel.
Records (records.json): each copies the stock graphic it replaces, read from the client's tiledata.mul, and adds
             PartialHue (0x00040000): the satchels OSI's 0xA272 "Ore_Satchel_east" (Container 0x00200000, weight 3,
             height 1) -> 0x00240000; the two bags OSI's bag 0xE76 (Container | ArticleA 0x00204000, weight 2,
             height 2) -> 0x00244000. Names 19 ASCII characters at most. Server copy: SatchelArt.Records.

Achievement category icons, gumps 22459-22468 (0x57BB-0x57C4) (cc-P241)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
Author:      the game-icons.net artists, converted to UO spell-icon style by Praxiiz: "1000+ Custom Spell Icons" 1.1.0,
             https://www.servuo.dev/archive/1000-custom-spell-icons.258/ (2014). Original at
             D:\UO\third-party\spell-icons-1000\ (bmp\<name>.bmp, 44 x 44, 24-bit). All ten shipped icons are by Lorc
             (http://lorcblog.blogspot.com): the set has no per-author folders, so each icon's author is the
             game-icons.net folder that serves it (https://game-icons.net/1x1/lorc/<name>.html, looked up 2026-10-21).
License:     Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 (CC BY 3.0), bmp\license.txt. Modification and commercial use allowed.
             REQUIRED: "Icons made by Lorc" (game-icons.net), and credit Praxiiz for the conversion, in the shard
             credits list.
Files:       22459 crossed-swords (Combat)   22460 open-book (Skills)          22461 compass (Exploration)
             22462 mining (Mining)           22463 anvil (Crafting)            22464 scroll-unfurled (Legacy)
             22465 magnifying-glass (Discovery)  22466 swap-bag (Collection)   22467 laurel-crown (League)
             22468 imp-laugh (Mischief, the hidden joke achievements)
What was done to the pixels: scripts\anchor-art-frames.py --black-transparent --keep-geometry. Pure black became
             transparent and the format became PNG; nothing else changed. The tool re-reads every PNG against its source.
Shown by:    the server's AchievementsGump (ClusterFAchievements.cs), beside each category's heading. No record needed.

League Hall decor, art 15592-15629 (0x3CE8-0x3D0D) (cc-P243)
-------------------------------------------------------------
Sold on the League shop's Hall page as account-bound deeds (server\customizations\LeagueShop\LeagueHall.cs). Three
community sets, none with a stated license; Chase 2026-10-21: use them, credit their authors in the credits list.
  15592-15601  RedRooster (Steven Armstrong), "Rooster's Display Cases" V.1.0, https://www.servuo.dev/archive/roosters-display-cases.1555/
               (D:\UO\third-party\display-cases\). His own drawing. Two shelves (Shelf1 facing south, Shelf2 east) and
               four inserts for each (Book 1/2, Book 5/6 partial hue, GEM1/2, GlassInsert1/2); a case is a shelf and an
               insert on one tile, each dyed on its own. Credit: RedRooster asks to be on the shard credits list.
  15602-15607  Hestia, "Trophys and Statues", https://www.servuo.dev/archive/trophys-and-statues.1804/
               (D:\UO\third-party\hestia-trophies\). Statues 1a/1b, 2a/2b (dragons, two facings), 5a (jeweled dragon),
               6a (gargoyle): rendered statues, not EA art. Credit Hestia.
  15608-15615  Hestia, the same pack: trophies Minotaur, Sabertooth, Troglodyte, Skull (1a/1b, north and west wall).
               EA-DERIVED (stock creatures on plaques, as her SOURCE.txt warns). Credit Hestia.
  15616-15629  Archaaz, "New Trophies and Heads", https://www.servuo.dev/archive/new-trophies-and-heads.1428/
               (D:\UO\third-party\trophies-heads\). Trophies Titan, Oni, Ophidian Matriarch, Terathan Matriarch,
               Paroxysmus (north and west wall) and heads Titan, Oni (two facings). EA-DERIVED ("using existing art",
               his words). Credit Archaaz.
Terms:       none stated for any of the three: community work, credit the author, ship only inside the player package
             or the private repo, do not repost. The EA-derived pieces ship as the earlier EA-derived art does (registry
             2071, the crow): only as our PNG override inside the player package, never as an EA file or part of one.
Pixels:      BMP to PNG and pure black made transparent (scripts\anchor-art-frames.py --black-transparent
             --keep-geometry); nothing else changed. Made by shard-migration notes\cc-P243-tools\hall_art.py.
Records:     shelves as OSI's bookcase 0xA97 (Impassable | ArticleA, height 12); inserts ArticleA, height 0 (Book 5/6
             PartialHue); statues as OSI's statue 0x1224 plus Impassable, height 20 (cc-P34's); trophies as OSI's trophy
             0x1E60 (ArticleA, height 0); mounted heads ArticleA, height 2. Server copy: LeagueHallArt.Records.

Flying loot, art 15536-15589 (0x3CB0-0x3CE5) (cc-P242)
--------------------------------------------------------
Author:      Clint Bellanger, "Flying Loot Animations", https://opengameart.org/content/flying-loot-animations (2010); base
             icon styles by Blarumyrran. Original at D:\UO\third-party\oga-flying-loot\ (23 strips, 384 x 128, six
             64 x 128 frames each, pink background; Blender sources beside them).
License:     CC-BY 3.0. Attribution required: credit Clint Bellanger (and Blarumyrran for the base icon styles) in the
             shard credits. CC-BY 3.0 asks that changes be stated: they are listed below and in every registry row.
Files:       six frames each, the base ID first (it carries our tiledata and animdata record):
               15536 longsword   15542 longbow   15548 staff    15554 steel_armor   15560 shield
               15566 ring        15572 gem       15578 health_potion             15584 clothes
             The other 14 strips (dagger, shortsword, greatsword, shortbow, greatbow, slingshot, wand, rod, greatstaff,
             buckler, leather_armor, mana_potion, boots, belt) are not shipped: the loot boxes use these nine kinds.
Changed:     (1) the pink background and (2) the pure-black drop shadow made transparent; (3) pixels with every
             channel under 8 lifted to (8,8,8), the darkest colour 16-bit art keeps; (4) not resized (the items are
             already UO's size); (5) cut to each animation's shared box by scripts\anchor-art-frames.py (centred, bottom
             row on the tile's tip). No recolouring, no redrawing. Made by shard-migration notes\cc-P242-tools\flying_loot.py.
Records:     tiledata as OSI's effect art (the sparkle 0x373A): Animation 0x01000000, weight 255, height 0; animdata
             frames 0-5 then 5 twice (the landed item rests), interval 1. Server copy: ClusterFFlyingLoot.Records.
Shown by:    the server's ClusterFFlyingLoot, as a location effect over a loot box's opener.

Winter decor, second block (cc-P266, F-22): art 13192-13238 (0x3388-0x33B6), gump 22469
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Two more of MrRiots' packs, downloaded 2026-10-18 by the daily art task and kept at D:\UO\third-party\
(originals in _zips\, SOURCE.txt in each folder). Both state their terms on the page; credit MrRiots wherever the
shard credits art. Both are built partly from OSI/EA assets: they ship only as our PNG overrides over placeholder
IDs, never as a part of an EA file.
  MrRiots, "Christmas Art for UO" (2023), https://www.servuo.dev/archive/mrriots-christmas-art-for-uo.2013/
           "Per usual, use these freely and edit them/label as you wish." The animated trees are his with thanks
           to Vorspire (his words). Folder mrriots-christmas: the two animated Christmas trees, the ribbon
           garlands, the tall candle stand, the short candle, the antler candelabra, the advent candles, the
           poinsettia, the potted tree, the gnome, the toy soldier and the dragon plushie.
  MrRiots, "Christmas Calendar [Gump/Item]" (2023), https://www.servuo.dev/archive/mrriots-christmas-calendar-gump-item.2069/
           "Use as you wish, edit as you wish, enjoy!" Folder mrriots-christmas-calendar: the calendar item
           (two facings) and the 400 x 400 calendar gump.
Every ID's file is in registry.csv. The frames of the animated pieces, in order:
  13192-13202  christmas tree (large)  Christmas Tree\xmastree 02.bmp .. 12.bmp
  13203-13213  christmas tree (small)  ChristmasTreeSmall\xmastree 02.bmp .. 12.bmp
  13216-13219  candle stand            TallCandle\1.bmp .. 4.bmp (Off.bmp not used)
  13220-13223  candle                  ShortCandle\1.bmp .. 4.bmp (off.bmp not used)
  13224-13227  antler candelabra       Antlier\Antlier.bmp, Antlier1.bmp, Antlier2.bmp, Antlier3.bmp
  13228-13231  advent candles          AdventCandles\1.bmp .. 4.bmp (the n-n.bmp facing and Off.bmp not used)
  gumps\22469.png                     AdventCalendar.bmp, the 25-door calendar (WinterAdventCalendarGump)
What was done to the pixels (notes\cc-P266-tools\convert_art.py, scripts\anchor-art-frames.py --keep-geometry
--black-transparent): the 24-bit BMP became a PNG, and pure black (0,0,0) became transparent, as UO art means it.
Nothing else: no recolouring, no scaling, no redrawing, no cut and no pad. The gump has no pure black pixel and
ships opaque. The tool re-reads every PNG and checks it against its source.
Records (records.json; the server's copy is ClusterFWinterDecorArt.Records), the flags from OSI's own art as read
from the client's tiledata.mul on 2026-10-21 (notes\cc-P266-tools\records.py): the large tree 0x01004041 height 20
(OSI's tree 0xCCA, Animation added); the small tree the same at height 10 (OSI's small banana tree 0xCAB); the
candle stand 0x05804040 height 15 light 29 (OSI's tall candelabra 0xB26); the candle 0x01804000 height 1 light 2
(OSI's lit candle 0xB1A); the antler candelabra 0x01808040 height 5 light 1 (OSI's candelabra 0xB1D); the advent
candles 0x01804000 height 3 light 2 (OSI's holiday candle 0x236E without PartialHue); the potted tree 0x00004040
height 5 (OSI's potted tree 0x11C8). Animdata: every animated piece runs its frames at interval 3, as OSI's lit
candle, candelabra and holiday candle do; the pack gives no timing of its own.
Not used from these packs: the second facings, the unlit frames, the table cloths, eggnog, hot cocoa, horseshoes,
the elk trophy, the figurines, the other plushies, the angel box, the second tall candle and the mistletoe. The
Hestia Christmas fireplace (hestia-christmas-fireplace) was left out: its page states no terms.
